reviewer: minor-free project owner, reciprocal read-only review
findings: The literal 13-slot program recursively traverses the represented least-significant-first word. The empty suffix and false-bit case returns the existing nil; the true-bit/nonempty-tail cases allocate one retained spine cell using the original flag pointer. Allocation is exactly the length of the resulting trim, with the original heap prefix unchanged.

Actual recursive caller frames restore saved registers and return to the supplied continuation. The top-level run starts with an empty stack, reaches the stated halt, preserves the source, and is transferred to the lower interpreter with the same instruction count and terminal-inclusive charge.

The 116-slot table embeds the existing 96-slot multiplication/addition code and 13-slot trim code. Only the original arithmetic halt is changed into the real normalization move, and the original trim halt into the actual return. Both table-preservation lemmas are restricted precisely to nonhalt instructions.

Both arithmetic branches preserve the original operands while returning the literal trim of the raw computed word, definitionally the existing addCanonical or mulCanonical result. The exact extension count includes raw allocations and retained trim spine cells.

The stored-input-length instruction bound and monotone completeBound are attached to the same lower-machine execution and its paid final halt; no independent semantic result is substituted for that run.
explicit_boundaries: Input BoolList representations, entry program counter, cursor equals heap length, initial width/heap bounds and empty top-level stack remain explicit.

Canonical means removal of high zero-bit padding in the existing natural-word arithmetic. These sources do not by themselves construct rational arithmetic, reduced fractions, graph path costs or a complete graph algorithm.

Source-only review does not replace the separate strict builds, allowed-axiom audits, actual-machine fixtures, official kernel replays or full remote CI. No runtime complexity of the whole graph algorithm is claimed.
